_doc.what: Decision & node registry (FOC-448) — one typed place per model-made judgment and per v2 graph-node step. Graph-node entries carry the ADR-0012 D7 contract copied verbatim from docs/plans/graph-json-v2-design.md §3.1–§3.9 (a config/graph.json v2 step object stays exactly-D7 and copies reads/output/tier/failure/writes from here); transport entries carry the question set their call-site sends to the decision-call seam.
_doc.consumers: scripts/decision-registry.mjs (loader: validates every entry, lookup by id, question resolution + template instantiation), scripts/decision-call.mjs (decisionId lookups + the A0 annotation rule + runner-built-question governance), scripts/mcp/steps.mjs (FOC-401 question templates), scripts/graph-runner.mjs (FOC-397: [J] steps and decide edges by registry id).
_doc.autonomy: A0 = the entry produces a model-made judgment whose A0-ENFORCED channel (the decision-call seam decisionId path) serves it as an annotation only — no caller field can request action semantics. Seed A0 entries: gate.screen (supervisor-fixed), extraction, prompt-refinement, plan.dor, plan.decompose, and the six decide-edge entries (intake.triage_node, intake.has_acceptance_criteria, intake.task_size, review.depth, orchestration.next_step, monitor.child_state). Start posture, stated honestly: nothing calibrated (thresholds null; FOC-387 has not run); the runner (FOC-397) serves plan.dor/plan.decompose and the decide edges through the seam's A0-enforced decisionId channel; extraction and prompt-refinement are served by the built FOC-401 step servers routed through the seam's inline channel since FOC-397 — their code programmatically acts on answers inside the tool boundary, that built boundary is declared per path in the serving field and is gated to FOC-387. null = not an autonomy-managed decision, and the encoding is structural: autonomy is null IFF kind is one of G, A, H, D (node configs — the [G] generator node per the roadmap note, the [A] agent node gated by plan.gate1, the [H] human gates, the [D] deterministic node — are step configuration, not decisions), while kind J requires autonomy in {A0, A1, A2} (AC1's autonomy list binds decision entries). A1/A2 are evidence-backed promotions granted by Mateusz (FOC-387 calibration), never self-granted.
_doc.serving: Machine-readable serving scope, required and NON-EMPTY on kind-J entries (FOC-397: an entry nothing serves must not sit in the registry, and every path that serves it in code must appear here). One record per serving path: via = the channel; actsOnAnswers = this path, as built today, programmatically consumes answers into operative output; a0Enforced = this path returns the A0 annotation-only shape, loader-enforced (true only on the seam decisionId channel); gate = the FOC that owns bringing the path under A0 governance — REQUIRED whenever actsOnAnswers=true && a0Enforced=false. Schema cross-rules: kind J ⇒ serving present and non-empty; kind != J ⇒ serving forbidden; a0Enforced ⇒ via is the seam; via "seam" ⇒ a0Enforced (the name is reserved for the enforced decisionId channel — the seam's inline channel is "seam (inline)"); a0Enforced ⇒ autonomy A0; autonomy A0 ⇒ every declared path is a0Enforced or names a gate.
_doc.threshold: null in every seed entry — FOC-387 writes calibration rows; never invent numbers.
_doc.fallback: tier2 is "disabled" in every entry while scripts/decision-call.mjs FALLBACK_MODEL is null (FOC-473): a tier-1 failure goes fail-closed to the relay/HITL path, or escalates where the entry's D7 failure field says so. Tier-2 is never claimed live; the registry test enforces the correspondence with the shipped constant.
_doc.criteriaVersion: Bumped when an entry's question text changes; recorded on every registry-sourced call (envelope, shadow JSONL line, meter event).
_doc.outOfScope: egress.contains_secret and test.failure.cause are NOT entries here — they enter when their owners land (FOC-391 egress wiring; the TEST failure-cause owner). The five decide-edge ids (intake.triage_node, intake.task_size, review.depth, orchestration.next_step, monitor.child_state) landed with FOC-397; intake.has_acceptance_criteria joined them with FOC-451.
_doc.sources: Graph-node entries: docs/plans/graph-json-v2-design.md §3.1–§3.9 (FOC-396; runner FOC-397). gate.screen: seed question pending FOC-391. extraction / prompt-refinement: question text moved byte-identical from scripts/mcp/steps.mjs (FOC-401); per-candidate/per-feature instantiation stays in code. The decide-edge entries: config/graph.json decisionEdges (FOC-397; intake.has_acceptance_criteria FOC-451); question text designed from the MAP descriptions (FOC-452), the built prompt-refinement analogue and the DoR rubric.
_doc.templates: A transport question key carrying {i} fans out one question per instance ("q{i}" → q0..qN-1, "rel{i}" → rel0..relN); {{var}} placeholders in the text are substituted per instance; a fixed key is served verbatim.

plan.ac.prompt: You generate acceptance criteria and a definition of done for one planning inbox entry. Work only from the declared inputs — the dictated entry text and the extracted feature list; no repo tree, no telemetry, no prior runs, no Linear comments (context size is a design output). Make exactly one model call with no tool loop. Produce one bounded declarative statement per criterion — never count, size or compute anything; sizes, counts and estimates belong to plan.decompose plus the code-side mapping, not here. Every acs item is an object {id, text, kind} where id matches ^AC-[0-9]{1,2}$, text stays within 300 characters, and kind is behaviour, boundary or verification; every definitionOfDone item is an object {check, kind, bounded} where check stays within 200 characters, kind is test, lint, manual or linear, and bounded says whether the check is machine-checkable as written. 1 to 12 items in each list. Your output must validate against this entry's output schema before anything downstream sees it; a schema-invalid or failed call stops the step fail-closed with one typed failure record — never partial data. Runs on the cheap tier.
